delights: The calorie arithmetic is uncanny. My six slots totalled 2295.92 kcal against my saved "targetKcal": 2296 — eight hundredths of a calorie off. After I swapped a meal it re-landed at 2292. Whatever else is wrong, it can hit a number.

The swap actually worked and made my day better. Alternates on the goat curry returned "recipeName":"Ground Beef & Rice Skillet" at "matchPct":100, and applying it dropped the day from $43.57 to $32.39 and my longest cook from 42 minutes to 20, while moving calories by 4. That is the one place the product felt like it was on my side.

Turkey & Swiss Roll-Ups is a real snack written by someone who has made food: "Lay turkey slices flat.","Place a strip of Swiss and a cucumber spear on each.","Roll tightly." — 27 g protein for 168 kcal and six minutes.

defects.what: A cooking instruction that is physically wrong — cottage cheese curdles and weeps if you heat it; you do not cook it. This is one of my four main meals and 275 g of it.
defects.snippet: "steps":["Cook the cottage cheese.","Serve over chickpea pasta with bell peppers."]

defects.what: My target looks like maintenance, not a lean bulk. I told it I weigh 97.9 kg and want 110.5 kg at 0.25 lb/wk. Using the app's own published numbers (occupation multiplier 1.2 for "unemployed-home", MET 7 for cardio) plus Mifflin-St Jeor, I burn roughly 2,310 kcal/day; a 0.25 lb/wk gain needs about +125, so ~2,435. It gave me 2,296 — slightly UNDER maintenance. Eating that, I gain nothing, and I am the one who asked to gain 12.6 kg.

There is no way to check that number. Nothing in the profile response shows BMR, TDEE, or how the target was derived, and /api/profile/engine, /api/engine and /api/profile/tdee all 404. I am asked to trust 2,296 with no visible math.

Sixty grams of thyme in one portion. That is a whole supermarket bunch, or roughly twenty tablespoons dried, in a single serving of curry — more thyme by weight than onion, potato and garlic combined. Reads like a scaled 'sprigs of thyme' line nobody sanity-checked.
defects.snippet: Goat Meat 270g | Jamaican Curry Powder 5g | Ground Ginger 1g | All-purpose Seasoning 1g | Allspice 1g | Onion 20g | Garlic 4g | Thyme 60g

defects.what: Half my main meals are the same sentence with the nouns swapped, and quinoa shows up in both. Add 300 g of cucumber across the day (140 g in meal 1, 160 g in the snack) and it is a repetitive day for something billed as balanced.
defects.snippet: "High-Protein White Fish & Cucumber with Quinoa" / "High-Protein Edamame & Onions with Quinoa"

defects.what: The swap list hides the only two things I was swapping for. I wanted out of the goat curry because it cost $21.62 and took 42 minutes at difficulty 7 — but alternates return no prepTimeMin, no costPerServing and no difficulty. I had to apply one blind to find out it was cheaper and faster. It also offered me a second cottage-cheese meal on a day that already had 275 g of cottage cheese in it.
defects.snippet: 1. Ground Beef & Rice Skillet — match 100% | prep=undefined cost=undefined difficulty=undefined

defects.what: The documented apply call rejected the recipe the app had just offered me, with a message that names nothing I can act on. I sent the recipeId and the two scales from its own alternates response; it complained about ingredients without saying it wanted the ingredient array echoed back. Second attempt with the whole object worked.
defects.snippet: PUT /api/plans/{planId}/slots/{slotId}/apply -> 400 {"error":"a slot needs at least one ingredient"}

defects.what: No way to tell it how I actually eat. I keep to low-FODMAP, and the nine dietary styles on offer have nothing for it — so the app cheerfully built me a day with 250 g edamame, 95 g onion, garlic, honey and chickpea pasta. I declared no hard exclusions, so nothing here is a broken wall and I am not calling it one, but a plan I physically cannot digest is no use to me and there was no field to say so.

Sloppy labelling that matters at the shop and the stove. A Jamaican dish is filed as Indian; olive oil is tagged as a carbohydrate; and 'Quinoa 170g' never says cooked or dry, though the chickpea pasta in the next meal is careful to say 'dry'. Dry vs cooked quinoa is a 400-calorie difference — I had to back it out of the slot's own kcal to know which one to buy.

Nobody flinched at my goal weight. 110.5 kg at 178 cm is BMI 34.9, and I am starting from an already-obese 30.9 — the app took it silently. Its own limits only guard the thin end, and rateAcknowledged is still false. A tool that tells me my protein source to the gram might mention that my goal takes me further into obesity.

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on the one meal I could not live with — Jamaican Curry Goat, $21.62, 42 minutes, difficulty 7, needing a 4-hour marinade, a 6QT pressure cooker and goat meat my supermarket does not carry — then swapped in the one normal option it offered, Ground Beef & Rice Skillet.
followUp.howItWent: Well, once I got past a 400 on my first apply — I sent the recipeId and scales from its own alternates response and got "a slot needs at least one ingredient", which explains nothing; echoing the entire alternate object back returned 200. The result was genuinely good: the day went from $43.57 to $32.39, my longest cook from 42 minutes to 20, difficulty 7 to 2, and total calories moved from 2295.92 to 2292 against a 2,296 target, with a dish that has real steps ("Brown the beef in a hot skillet, breaking it up as it cooks."). My irritation is that alternates never showed me the cost or the time, so the improvement I was chasing was invisible until after I committed.

verdict: It nails my calorie number to within a rounding error and its swap tool genuinely rescued my day, but the number it is nailing looks like maintenance rather than the surplus a 97.9-to-110.5 kg lean bulk needs, it won't show me the math behind it, and half the meals are two-line templates — one of which tells me to cook cottage cheese.
